target.name: BotBuilt
target.founder: Barrett Ames, Colin Devine, Brent Wadas

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $12M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
BotBuilt, a seed-stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Barrett Ames, Colin Devine, and Brent Wadas, has raised $12.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of five private construction-tech companies including Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral. No public market comparables exist in this subsector, limiting the ability to benchmark against listed peers.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $12M raised proxy, reflecting typical valuation step-ups observed in seed-to-next-stage transitions within the sector. This approach yields an implied valuation of $31M. Given the single-method constraint and absence of revenue multiples or DCF data points in the dataset, this represents the primary analytical anchor rather than a triangulated consensus across divergent methodologies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $36M (high), with a median point of $31M. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the five-company peer set—particularly whether those comparables reflect similar burn rates, customer concentration, or technical maturity—and the absence of margin profiles or growth trajectory data to validate the 2.5x multiplier as appropriate to BotBuilt's specific execution risk profile. Stage progression alone is a blunt instrument; incorporation of additional methods (revenue comps, precedent transactions) would materially strengthen conviction in any narrow valuation point.
